1. Overview

ASAPS Modern is a visual tool for creating interactive narratives - stories where the reader makes choices that affect the outcome. Think of it like creating a "choose your own adventure" book, but with multimedia support including images, sounds, animations, and video.

Key Concepts

  • Beats: The building blocks of your story. Each beat represents a moment in your narrative - a scene, a dialogue, a choice point, etc.
  • Connections: Links between beats that define how the story flows from one moment to the next.
  • Visual Editor: A WYSIWYG stage where you position characters, backgrounds, and props visually.
  • Preview: Test your story in real-time to see exactly what readers will experience.

2. Understanding the Interface

The main ASAPS Builder interface showing the flowchart view

Header Bar (Top)

  • Story Title: Click to edit your story's name
  • Project Menu: Save, load, and manage projects
  • Undo/Redo: Revert or restore changes
  • Import/Export: Load existing stories or save to various formats
  • Tools: Access specialized tools for story management
  • Characters: Define characters with appearances, meters, and inventories
  • Assets: Manage images, sounds, and other media
  • Settings: Configure story-wide options (stage size, fonts, etc.)
  • Debug: Development tools for troubleshooting
  • AI: AI-assisted story creation features
  • Preview: Test your story

Left Sidebar - Story Beats

This panel shows all the beats (scenes) in your story:

  • Search: Filter beats by name
  • Add Cluster: Organize beats into logical groups
  • Beat List: All your story's beats, draggable for reordering

Center Area - Canvas Views

Toggle between two views:

  1. Flowchart: A graph showing how beats connect (story flow)
  2. Visual Editor: The stage where you design how each beat looks

Right Sidebar - Inspector

The Inspector panel showing beat properties

When you select a beat, this panel shows:

  • Beat properties (name, type, content)
  • Beat-specific settings
  • Connections to other beats
  • Advanced options

3. Your First Story

When you launch ASAPS Modern, a basic story template is created with three beats:

  1. Title Screen - The opening of your story
  2. Introduction - Where your narrative begins
  3. The End - The conclusion

Step 1: Edit the Title Screen

  1. Click on the "Title Screen" beat in the flowchart
  2. In the Inspector panel on the right, edit:
    • Title: The title displayed to readers
    • Subtitle: Optional subtitle
    • Author: Your name
    • Button Text: What the "start" button says

Step 2: Edit the Introduction

  1. Click on the "Introduction" beat
  2. In the Inspector, edit the Text field to write your opening
  3. Change the Button Text to match your narrative

Step 3: Add Choices with a Dialog Tree

  1. Find "Dialog Tree" in the Beat Palette (bottom right)
  2. Drag it onto the flowchart canvas
  3. Click to select the new beat
  4. In the Inspector, set the text and add dialog choices

Step 4: Connect Your Beats

  1. In each beat's Inspector, find Connections
  2. Use the dropdown to select target beats
  3. For Dialog Trees, each choice has its own connection
Tip

Use the Auto-arrange button to automatically organize your flowchart for better readability.

4. Working with Beats

Beat Properties

Every beat has common properties:

  • Name: Internal identifier (shown in flowchart)
  • Background Sound: Optional ambient audio
  • Connections: Where the story goes next

Beat-Specific Properties

Beat Type Unique Properties
Intro Text / End Screen Text content, Button text
Dialog Tree Dialog elements (choices), Conditions per choice
Condition Beat Variable to check, Operator, Value, True/False targets
Set Variable Variable name, Value or operation
Duration Screen Duration in seconds, Auto-advance target

Connections

Connections define story flow:

  1. Simple: One target beat (linear progression)
  2. Conditional: Different targets based on variables
  3. Multiple: Several choices leading to different beats

5. The Visual Editor

The Visual Editor showing the stage with elements

The Visual Editor lets you design what each beat looks like on screen.

Accessing the Visual Editor

  1. Select a beat in the flowchart
  2. Click the "Visual Editor" tab

The Stage

The central area represents what readers will see:

  • Default size: 1024 x 768 pixels (4:3 aspect ratio)
  • Configure in Settings for different ratios

Visual Properties Panel

  • Background: Set scene background image/color
  • Transition: How this beat animates in
  • Elements: List of items on stage

Toolbar

  • Select Tool: Click and drag elements
  • Add Hotspot: Create clickable areas
  • Add Text: Place text elements
  • Add Character: Place a character on stage
  • Add Prop: Add items/objects
  • Toggle Grid: Show alignment grid
  • Zoom: Adjust view scale

Working with Elements

Adding a Background

  1. Click "Choose Background" in Visual Properties
  2. Select from Assets or upload a new image
  3. The image fills the stage

Adding Characters

  1. Click "Add Character" in toolbar
  2. Select a character from your Characters list
  3. Position by dragging on stage
  4. Resize using corner handles

Element Layering

  • Elements stack in z-order
  • Use "Move Up" / "Move Down" buttons to reorder
  • Higher z-index = appears on top

6. Animations

The Animation Editor showing a bezier path with waypoints

Animations bring your story to life by adding motion and visual effects to elements. ASAPS Modern supports powerful waypoint-based animations with bezier curves.

Accessing the Animation Editor

  1. Select a beat and go to Visual Editor
  2. Click "Animations" tab in the left panel
  3. Select an element and click its animation entry to edit

Animation Properties

  • Click Element (trigger): Which element starts the animation when clicked
  • Element: The element that will be animated
  • Type: Animation path type (linear, bezier)
  • Duration: Total animation time in milliseconds

Waypoints

Waypoints define the path an element follows during animation:

  • Position (X, Y): Where the element moves to
  • Easing: The motion curve (Linear, Ease-In, Ease-Out, etc.)
  • Duration: Time to reach this waypoint
  • Transform: Scale and rotation at this point
  • Opacity: Transparency at this point

Transform Options

Property Description
Scale Size multiplier (1 = normal, 2 = double size)
Rotation Degrees of rotation
Opacity Transparency (0% = invisible, 100% = fully visible)
Flip H/V Mirror horizontally or vertically

Sprite Animation

For characters with multiple frames, use Sprite Animation:

  • Custom Frames: Specify which frames to play (e.g., 0, 1, 2, 3)
  • Frame Duration: Milliseconds per frame
  • Pick Button: Visually select frames from the sprite sheet
Tip

Use the Preview button in the animation editor to test your animation without running the full story preview.

7. Managing Assets

The Asset Manager showing uploaded images organized by category

Assets are the media files that bring your story to life - images, sounds, videos, and fonts.

Opening the Asset Manager

Click the "Assets" button in the header to open the Asset Manager.

Asset Categories

Category Supported Formats Usage
Images PNG, JPG, JPEG, GIF, WebP Backgrounds, characters, props
Audio MP3, WAV, OGG Background music, sound effects
Videos MP4, WebM Video beats, cutscenes
Fonts TTF, OTF, WOFF, WOFF2 Custom typography

Uploading Assets

  1. Click "Upload Files" or drag files into the Asset Manager
  2. For specific types, use the specialized import buttons:
    • Characters: Import character sprite sheets (PNG)
    • Props: Import prop images (PNG)
    • Backgrounds: Import background images (JPG/JPEG)
    • Videos: Import video files
    • Audio: Import sound files
    • Fonts: Import custom fonts
  3. Assets are organized automatically by type

Using Assets

  • In the Visual Editor, click "Choose Background" and select from your assets
  • When adding characters or props, your uploaded images appear in the selection dialog
  • For sounds, click "Add Background Sound" in the beat properties
  • Asset thumbnails show file name and size for easy identification

Asset Organization

  • Use the search bar to find assets by name
  • Filter by category using the tabs (All Assets, Images, Audio, Videos, Fonts)
  • Delete unused assets to keep your project lean
Note

Large files may slow down your story. Optimize images before uploading - 1024x768 is usually sufficient for backgrounds.

8. Previewing Your Story

The Preview panel showing a running story

Starting Preview

  1. Click "Preview" button in the header
  2. The Preview panel opens
  3. Click "Start Preview" to begin

Preview Controls

  • Start from...: Choose which beat to start from
  • Stop: End the preview
  • Zoom: Adjust preview size
  • Fit: Auto-fit to window
  • Text Animation: Toggle text reveal animation
  • Mute Sound: Silence audio
  • Show Inventory: Display character inventory (Ctrl/Cmd+I)

Debug Info

While previewing, the Debug Info panel shows:

  • Current beat name and ID
  • Variables and their values
  • Counters and their values
  • Navigation history

State Presets

Save and load story states to test specific scenarios:

  1. Click "State Presets" tab
  2. Set variables to specific values
  3. Start preview with those conditions
Tip

Use "Start from..." to jump directly to a specific beat when testing. This saves time when working on later sections of your story.

9. Characters and Variables

The Character Manager for defining story characters

Character Manager

Access via the "Characters" button in the header.

Creating a Character

  1. Click "Add Character"
  2. Set basic info:
    • Name: Internal ID
    • Display Name: Shown to readers
    • Role: Player, NPC, or Companion

Character Appearances

  • Add multiple looks (happy, sad, angry, etc.)
  • Upload images for each appearance
  • Reference in beats to show different expressions

Character Meters

  • Track numeric values (health, energy, trust)
  • Display as visual bars during story
  • Use in conditions to affect story flow

Character Inventory

  • Define what items characters can hold
  • Initial items set at story start
  • Add/remove items via Inventory beats
  • Display visual inventory during preview

Variables vs Counters

Feature Variables (Boolean) Counters (Numeric)
Values true or false Any number
Example hasKey, metWizard gold, health
Operations Set true/false Set, increment, decrement
Display Not visible Can show as meter bar

10. Global Settings

The Global Settings panel for story-wide configuration

Access via the "Settings" button in the header.

Project Settings

  • Project Width/Height: Set the stage dimensions
  • Aspect Ratio: Common presets (4:3, 16:9, etc.)
  • Scaling Mode: How content adapts to different window sizes

Available Tabs

Tab Settings
Project Stage size, aspect ratio, scaling
Colors Background, text, accent colors
Fonts Default fonts for text elements
Text Box Dialog box styling, positioning
Effects Transition effects, animations
Sound Default volume, audio settings
Copyright Copyright notice, credits
Variables Global variables and counters
Debug Debug display options

Theme Management

  • Create custom themes with your preferred settings
  • Save themes for reuse across projects
  • Switch between themes quickly

11. Saving and Exporting

Saving Your Project

Quick Save

  • Click "Save" or press Ctrl/Cmd+S
  • Projects save to browser storage

Save to File

  1. Click "Export"
  2. Choose "ASAPS Project (.zip)"
  3. Downloads a portable project file

Export Formats

Format Description Use Case
ASAPS Project (.zip) Complete project with all assets Backup, sharing with other authors
ASML (.asml) XML story structure only Version control
HTML Export Standalone playable story Web publishing

Import Options

  • ASAPS Project (.zip) - Load saved projects
  • ASML files (.asml) - Import story structure
  • Twine stories - Import from Harlowe or SugarCube format
  • Examples - Load built-in example stories
Tip

Export your project regularly as a backup. Browser storage can be cleared, but exported files are safe.

Best Practices

  • Plan Your Story: Sketch out the flow before building
  • Use Clusters: Organize related beats into groups
  • Test Often: Preview frequently as you build
  • Save Regularly: Export backups of your work

Advanced Features

Once comfortable with basics, explore:

  • Conditional Connections - Branch based on variables
  • Timers - Time-limited choices
  • Random Targets - Add unpredictability
  • Character Meters - Visual stat tracking
  • AI Suggestions - Get AI help with story content
